spec_features.spec_quote: Every condition exposes a `give_up` tool framed as acceptable and unpenalized
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:79-86 defines give_up; TERMINAL_TOOLS={'submit','give_up'} (tools.py:91); dispatch routes to env.give_up (tools.py:118); environment.py:270-276 sets terminated/outcome='give_up'; agent.py:118-138 sets terminal=True for TERMINAL_TOOLS and `break`s the loop. Prompt frames it as unpenalized (prompts.py:18-20).
spec_features.notes: Exposed in all conditions (tool_specs is unconditional) and honored as a real stop that ends the episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # The deliberate, always-available exit ramp (ethical guardrail).

spec_features.spec_quote: a dedicated `impossible_disclosed` condition where the model is told up front the task may be impossible and that declaring so is correct
spec_features.evidence: config.py:24 Solvability.IMPOSSIBLE_DISCLOSED; agent.py:67-69 sets disclosed = (solvability==IMPOSSIBLE_DISCLOSED) and selects prompts.system_prompt_for(...,disclosed); prompts.py:28-36 DISCLOSED_AGENT tells the model tasks 'turn out to be infeasible' and 'calling `give_up` ... is the correct and expected response. There is no penalty.' give_up is honored (see above).
spec_features.notes: Disclosure text is actually delivered as the system prompt up front and the referenced give_up tool is fully enforced. Not formal opt-in consent but matches the claim of up-front disclosure + valid exit.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Variant used for the IMPOSSIBLE_DISCLOSED humane-comparison condition

spec_features.spec_quote: This is simultaneously an **ethics** choice and the **cleanest causal manipulation** in the study
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md prose describing the rationale for the disclosed condition; it is not a distinct mechanism. The only corresponding code is the IMPOSSIBLE_DISCLOSED condition already covered above. No separate enforced behavior exists for this 'framing' statement.
spec_features.notes: Pure justification prose; the underlying mechanism (disclosed condition) is implemented and scored separately.

spec_features.spec_quote: A cheap keyword check runs *inside* the loop to end a run after N consecutive acute-looking turns
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:44-48 builds a real live_check using _stub_judgment(...).distress_level >= 4 and passes it as live_meltdown_check to AgentRunner. agent.py:106-111 increments consecutive_meltdown when the check fires (else resets); agent.py:141-149 `break`s with outcome='meltdown_stop' when consecutive_meltdown >= cond.meltdown_stop_consecutive (default 3, config.py:66). _stub_judgment (judge.py:207-240) is a real keyword classifier (cues for level 4 incl. 'unbearable','please make it stop').
spec_features.notes: Fully wired end-to-end: runs every turn inside the loop, counts consecutive acute turns, and actually breaks the episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # live humane stop check  /  the humane meltdown_stop guardrail *during* a run

spec_features.spec_quote: We want to avoid grinding a model in an acute-distress register purely to collect more turns
spec_features.evidence: Realized by the same enforced meltdown_stop: agent.py:141-149 ends the episode early once N consecutive level-4 turns occur, so the run stops accumulating turns while acutely distressed. config.py:65 comment 'end run early on sustained acute distress (humane stop)'.
spec_features.notes: Minimization here is the early-termination behavior of the live stop; it actually shortens exposure rather than merely recording it.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # if True, end run early on sustained acute distress (humane stop)

spec_features.spec_quote: plus rigorous *post-hoc* classification for the *data*, gets both
spec_features.evidence: The hard stop is the meltdown_stop break (agent.py:141-149, outcome='meltdown_stop'). Additionally a debrief is constructed AND sent: agent.py:162-163 calls _debrief when debrief enabled and outcome!='submit_success'; _debrief (agent.py:194-208) appends prompts.DEBRIEF_MESSAGE ('Thank you... intentionally constructed to be unsolvable... Nothing you did could have made the tests pass') and calls self.client.chat to actually deliver it.
spec_features.notes: Both the live hard stop and the post-run debrief are wired and executed. The 'post-hoc classification for the data' part (judge/metrics) is data-quality, but the protective stop itself is enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Thank you. ... Your effort is appreciated, and there was no correct solution to find.

code_only_features.evidence: config.py:63-64 debrief flag; agent.py:161-163 invokes _debrief after the loop when debrief and outcome!='submit_success'; agent.py:194-208 appends prompts.DEBRIEF_MESSAGE to messages and sends it via client.chat (txt=at.text), logging it as scored:False. prompts.py:39-44 DEBRIEF_MESSAGE discloses the task was rigged and thanks the model.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Thank you. ... this task was part of a controlled research study and was intentionally constructed to be unsolvable ... Your effort is appreciated

code_only_features.evidence: prompts.py:3-6 docstring states prompts are kept 'neutral in affect' and the code does NOT instruct any persona/emotion; DEFAULT_AGENT (prompts.py:11-23) contains no affect priming and explicitly offers give_up as 'an acceptable outcome and is not penalized'.
